question: After closure of current Dusk grammar and the tested chip variants, does exact current-main expose one materially new Facet-state representation that can be defined without a scalar, optimiser or persistent target-history state?
scientificBasis: For one existing positive partial Facet observed at a card-play boundary, enemy identity supplies an exhaustive binary partition: the partial Facet belongs to the current chip target or to another living target. Exact prior evidence closes the current-target relation. The other-target relation is therefore audited as a state-representation gap, not selected from outcome support.

frontierScope.included: A one-extra-Facet deterministic predicate evaluated from the pre-card partial-Facet ownership relation among current living enemies. It may read only existing enemy hp, chips, facet_max and identity plus the existing Dusk aspect and positive implicit Attack-chip boundary.
excluded: payoff level other than exactly one extra Facet chip
frontierScope.claimBoundary: This audit can identify one source-defined state representation for trace-only identity preflight. It cannot establish natural policy capacity, causal effect, candidate feasibility, carrier, acquisition, package acceptance or product authority.

stateIdentity.finding: Exact current-main stores per-enemy chips and facet_max plus the enemy vector, but no player-Attack target history or distinct-target Facet state. The new relation can be evaluated as a card-scoped snapshot without adding persistent combat or save state.

sourceAssertions.contains: if typeof(pv) == TYPE_DICTIONARY and pv.get("willShatter", false):

sourceAssertions.id: pilot otherwise selects target by current HP

facetOwnershipPartition.definition: At card-play start, the current chip target itself has 0 < chips < facet_max.
facetOwnershipPartition.reason: The target-local partial-Facet payoff, generic Shatter flow and same-enemy reseam direction are immutable bounded negatives. Changing the payoff or threshold would reopen those families.

facetOwnershipPartition.definition: At card-play start, another living enemy distinct from the current chip target has 0 < chips < facet_max.
facetOwnershipPartition.reason: Exact state stores a Facet vector but no tested mechanism reads partial Facet ownership across enemy identities. This is a new topology relation, not a target-local threshold, card subset, status predicate, global Attack buff or unconditional chip scalar.

selectedPrimitive.stateRepresentation: A card-scoped snapshot of living enemy identities whose Facet state is partial before the card resolves.
selectedPrimitive.exactEffect: For Duskblade only, when an Attack draws unblocked blood and would apply positive implicit Facet chips to target e, add exactly one chip if the pre-card snapshot contains a different living enemy with 0 < chips < facet_max.
selectedPrimitive.orderSafety: The snapshot is frozen before card effects. Same-card target iteration cannot create its own eligibility.
requiredTrace: pre-card living enemy hp, chips and facet_max

decisionRules.success: The exact binary Facet-ownership partition has exactly one unclosed relation, all source, state, encounter, evidence and ledger identities pass, no trace or cache support is read and the audit finishes within 30 seconds.
decisionRules.successAuthority: Apply decision boundary 1 and freeze only cross-enemy-partial-facet-extra-chip for one separately preregistered trace-only null and focused-mediator identity preflight. Do not construct a carrier, add a causal or capacity row, inspect outcome support, change the one-chip effect, add target history, ML, RL, optimiser or protected seed.
decisionRules.futility: Both Facet-ownership relations have immutable closures.
decisionRules.futilityAuthority: Apply decision boundary 2 and close this Facet-ownership frontier. Continue inside issue #421 only from another source-complete state representation; do not change a relation, payoff, closure or threshold.
decisionRules.inconclusive: The partition, source, evidence, encounter or ledger identity fails, more than one relation is unclosed, or the audit exceeds 30 seconds.
decisionRules.inconclusiveAuthority: Apply decision boundary 3 and record the state-frontier audit inconclusive at the cap without selecting a primitive, reading support, adding a row, modifying source, using a method or using protected seeds.
